# C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic

*Level 1 card. 5 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires. This includes selecting algorithms with worse complexity (suboptimal choice), failing to prune, order, or memoize subproblem exploration (inefficient decomposition), using recursion where iterative solutions are straightforward and more efficient in Python (avoidable recursion), performing operations in a suboptimal order (inefficient ordering), and failing to simplify inputs before applying expensive operations (unsimplified operation).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires | replace the algorithm with one whose complexity fits the input size | yes, scales with input |
| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused | memoise overlapping subproblems, prune what cannot contribute, or reorder to prune sooner | yes, scales with input |
| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a linear recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one | convert linear recursion to a loop with an explicit accumulator | yes, scales with call count |
| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data | run the cheap, reducing operation before the expensive one | yes, scales with input |
| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires | simplify the input or the operation using a fact about the values | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C7.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C7.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C7.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C7.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C7.S5.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
